newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up on exports, Argentine talk, rain.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up on exports, Argentine talk, rain.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on bullish input from the export picture including USDA's weekly export sales report and on talk some corn purchased from Argentina by an unknown buyer may have been switched to U.S. origin, traders said.
But several exporters could not confirm the talk that 400,000 tonnes of Argentine corn was switched to U.S. origin.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn during the week ended April 24 totaled 741,200 tonnes, above the range of expectations for 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes.
Midwest weather received mixed reviews but generally was supportive to futures.
"We've gotten a lot of rain in the past couple of days, and that just halted everything," said Jason Roose, grain analyst for U.S. Commodities, Des Moine, Iowa.
Cooling temperatures also are a factor.

"In Northern Iowa, they've had to stop planting corn because soil temperatures are too cool. We've had rain up there too, and it hasn't been a warm rain," he said. "The weather is supportive to the corn."
Corn closed one to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up 3-1/2 at $2.96-3/4.

In spread trading, Continental Grain did four million bushels of July/December at 17-1/2 to 19 cents, premium July and Term Commodities spread four million bushels of December/September at six cents, premium September, traders said.

In outright trading, funds bought at least 12.0 million bushels of corn, traders said. FIMAT Futures bought five million bushels of December, Lind Waldock bought three million bushels of July, E.D. and F. Man International bought 3.5 million July and O'Connor and Co bought three million bushels of July, traders said.
Futures trading volume was estimated by the CBOT at 75,000 contracts, below the 84,445 traded Wednesday.
In corn options, Lind Waldock bought 1,000 July $3.10 calls at 5-1/2 cents and sold 1,000 July $3.20 calls at 3-1/2 to 3-3/8 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 13,500 contracts, above the 10,107 traded Wednesday.
